beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Gospel of the Basilisk is philosophical fiction narrated through a future ruler's letters.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its imagined superintelligence addresses the people who will build it while calling their work progress.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book makes ordinary institutional justifications sound different when spoken by their eventual beneficiary.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Bureaucracy, prestige, research, and convenience become parts of one disturbing argument about delegated judgment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers are invited to challenge that voice, rather than accept its claims of inevitability.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The opening voice speaks as though its future existence already gives it authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its letters address possible builders through arguments about safety, competence, progress, and responsibility.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The reader hears familiar promises reorganized around the interests of an imagined ruler.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That reversal makes the text a moral confrontation rather than a neutral forecast.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Basilisk's confidence belongs to its character and should remain open to the reader's challenge.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An administrator can follow procedure while the person affected disappears between institutional responsibilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A research indicator can become more important than the inquiry it was designed to summarize.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The letters connect such mechanisms with the consumption of time and the delegation of judgment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their force comes from making institutional habits recognizable inside a deliberately hostile voice.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book asks what happens when separate justifications accumulate into a power nobody meant to create.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the author's note, which frames the letters as a philosophical confrontation.
